title: Disallowing Recurrence Rule Modification on Single-Instance Edit (Range.NONE)

citations.verbatim_quote: If present, this JSCalendar object represents one occurrence of a recurring JSCalendar object. If present, the "recurrenceRules" and "recurrenceOverrides" properties MUST NOT be present.

A pointer in the PatchObject MUST be ignored if it starts with one of the following prefixes:

   *  @type

   *  excludedRecurrenceRules

   *  method

   *  privacy

   *  prodId

   *  recurrenceId

   *  recurrenceIdTimeZone

   *  recurrenceOverrides

   *  recurrenceRules

A VEVENT (or VTODO) component is a recurrence override if it has the RECURRENCE-ID property set, and the iCalendar object contains a VEVENT (or VTODO) component that does not have the RECURRENCE-ID but the RRULE property set, and the UID property values of the two components are equal. The component without the RECURRENCE-ID property is in that case referred to as the "main component".

rationale: Per RFC 8984 Sections 4.3.1 and 4.3.5 and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Section 2.1.2, a single recurrence instance override represents a single occurrence and MUST NOT define its own `recurrenceRules` (RRULE). Changing the recurrence rule of a series is only meaningful when editing the entire series (no recurrence_id) or splitting the series (THISANDFUTURE range), or when converting a non-recurring component into a recurring one. Consequently, attempting to modify the RRULE during a single-instance edit (where recurrence_id is specified and range is NONE) is invalid, while supplying an unchanged RRULE in a patch payload is treated as a no-op and omitted from the single-instance override component.
store_implication: When a single-instance edit is invoked (with a recurrence identifier and single-instance range): (1) if the patch specifies an RRULE that differs from the master component's RRULE (or if re-editing an already-overridden single instance with a non-null RRULE), the calendar store MUST reject the operation with an error; (2) if the patch specifies an RRULE identical to the master component's RRULE, the store treats the RRULE in the patch as a no-op and still sets RRULE to null on the single-instance override component; (3) when editing a component as a whole (no recurrence identifier), setting or updating RRULE is permitted.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Attempting to edit a single occurrence (e.g., recurrence_id='20220905T090000' with single-instance range) of a FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=3 series with a patch containing RRULE='FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3' MUST be rejected with an error.

Re-editing an already-overridden single instance (where RECURRENCE-ID is present and RRULE is null) with a non-null RRULE and single-instance range MUST also be rejected with an error (it MUST NOT turn the single-instance override into a sub-series carrying both RECURRENCE-ID and RRULE).
Editing an entire series (recurrence_id=None) with a patch whose RRULE equals the existing master RRULE is allowed as a no-op on RRULE and MUST preserve the RRULE on the master series.

scenarios.name: reject_different_rrule_on_single_instance_edit
scenarios.description: Attempting to change RRULE when editing a single instance with Range.NONE is rejected with an error and leaves the calendar unchanged.

operation.expect_error: Can't update single instance with rrule
